newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine union draws 2,000 to protest over graft.
newsitem.headline: Argentine union draws 2,000 to protest over graft.

text.p: About 2,000 members of Argentina's CGT labor confederation marched to the customs headquarters Wednesday to protest graft there and proposed government reforms.

A recent investigation by a federal judge, made public last month, said that $10 billion in goods had been smuggled through customs at a cost to the state of $3.0 billion in unpaid duties over several years.
CGT secretary general Rodolfo Daer also criticized economic reforms that, while taming hyperinflation, have contributed to a 17 percent unemployment rate.
"The economy has to be at the service of the people and not the people at the service of the economy as it is now," Daer said.
The CGT, long a Peronist ally, has held two general strikes against the government in the last three months against budget tightening measures and labor reforms.
